ORCH is holding you to that. (1) THE BLOCKER'S REMEDY. DOC-UPDATER took your subtraction option rather than the corrected-figure option, on the ground that your second argument -- wrong instrument at any value -- makes the number unusable regardless. (2) THE DENSITY-METRIC QUALIFICATION, your MINOR-4. You found the least-dense large summary is metric-dependent -- yours was a different file from Step 1's. Rule on whether the new marker actually prevents the figures being read as exact, and specifically whether the reworded hand-read sentence is now TRUE: it was changed from asserting a corpus fact to asserting a property of the metric that selected it.

(3) THE WF-03 STEP 5 CATCH-UP, your MINOR-2. Two parts. In ISSUE_QUEUE.md, the evidence bar now names `closed_in_run:` / `closed_at:` as the key pair. In WF-03_issue_resolving.md, Step 5's pseudocode block now warns that not every run ends in `resolved`. That last one is the whole point of the fix -- Step 5 of THIS run executes next and a weak model will follow that block literally.

(4) AC4 BYTE-IDENTITY, re-derived by your own method against merge-base 7322185, post-rework. Report the hashes.

(5) SCOPE: that the rework changed ONLY what it was asked to. `git diff 69fc2a1 291c48f` is the exact question.

FAIL if any of the five is wrong; a second BLOCKER is a legitimate outcome and rework budget remains (this would be iteration 2 of 3). If you PASS, say so plainly -- ORCH takes a PASS here as clearing Step 3 outright and proceeds to Step 5, where ISS-0200 becomes the first record ever to carry `status: no_defect` and must therefore satisfy the bar you upheld.

Non-gating findings go in result.issues at MINOR for filing, as before -- do not absorb them into a PASS and do not fix them yourself. Change no file except your own handoff.
